1.w: Therefore [there is] now no condemnation to those in Christ Jesus.

2.w: For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus set you free from the law of sin and death.

3.w: For what the law [was] incapable of in that it was weak through the flesh, God, having sent His Son in the likeness of flesh of sin and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh,

4.w: so that the righteous requirement of the law might be fulfilled in us, those not walking according to the flesh but according to the Spirit.

5.w: For those being according to the flesh mind the [things] of the flesh, but those according to the Spirit the [things] of the Spirit.

6.w: For the mind of the flesh [is] death, but the mind of the Spirit [is] life and peace,

7.w: because the mind of the flesh [is] hostility toward God; for it does not subject itself to the law of God, for [it is] not even able.

8.w: And those being in the flesh are not able to please God.

9.w: But you⁺ are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if indeed the Spirit of God dwells in you⁺; and if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, this one is not of Him.

10.w: But if Christ [is] in you⁺, the body [is] indeed dead because of sin, but the spirit [is] life because of righteousness.

11.w: And if the Spirit of the One having raised Jesus out from the dead dwells in you⁺, the One having raised Christ Jesus out from the dead will also make alive your⁺ mortal bodies through His Spirit, the One dwelling in you⁺.

12.w: So then, brothers, we are debtors, not to the flesh, to live according to the flesh.

13.w: For if you⁺ live according to the flesh, you⁺ are about to die; but if by the Spirit you⁺ put to death the deeds of the body, you⁺ will live.

14.w: For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are sons of God.

15.w: For you⁺ did not receive a spirit of slavery again unto fear, but you⁺ received the Spirit of adoption as sons, in whom we cry, “Abba! Father!”

16.w: The Spirit Himself testifies with our spirit that we are children of God,

17.w: and if children, also heirs: heirs indeed of God, and co-heirs of Christ, if indeed we suffer with [Him], so that we may also be glorified with [Him].

18.w: For I reckon that the sufferings of the present time [are] not comparable to the glory about to be revealed in us.

19.w: For the eager expectation of the creation eagerly awaits the revelation of the sons of God.

20.w: For the creation was subjected to futility, not willingly, but because of the One having subjected [it], in hope

21.w: that the creation itself will also be set free from the bondage of decay, into the freedom of the glory of the children of God.

22.w: For we know that all the creation groans together and travails together until now.

23.w: And not only [so], but we ourselves, even having the firstfruit of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, eagerly awaiting adoption as sons, the redemption of our body.

24.w: For in hope we were saved, but hope being seen is not hope. For does anyone hope for what he sees?

25.w: But if we hope for what we do not see, we eagerly await in perseverance.

26.w: Now likewise also, the Spirit joins to help in our weakness; for we do not know the [things] that we should pray for as it is necessary, but the Spirit Himself intercedes with inexpressible groanings.

27.w: And the One searching hearts knows what [is] the mind of the Spirit, because He intercedes for the saints according to God.

28.w: And we know that God works together all things for good to those loving God, to those being called according to purpose,

29.w: because whom He foreknew, He also predestined [to be] conformed to the image of His Son, for Him to be firstborn among many brothers.

30.w: And whom He predestined, these also He called; and whom He called, these also He justified; and whom He justified, these also He glorified.

31.w: What then will we say to these things? If God [is] for us, who [can be] against us—

32.w: He who indeed did not spare [His] own Son, but delivered Him up for us all, how will He not also with Him graciously give us all things?

33.w: Who will bring an accusation against the chosen ones of God? God [is] the One justifying.

34.w: Who [is] the one condemning? Christ Jesus the One having died, now rather having been raised, [is] He who is also at the right hand of God, and who is interceding for us.

35.w: Who will separate us from the love of Christ? Will tribulation or distress or persecution or famine or nakedness or danger or sword?

36.w: As it has been written: “For Your sake we face death all the day; we were reckoned as sheep of slaughter.”

37.w: But in all these things we are more than conquerors through the One having loved us.

38.w: For I am persuaded that neither death nor life, nor angels nor principalities, nor things present nor things about to be, nor powers,

39.w: nor height nor depth, nor any other created thing, will be able to separate us from the love of God that [is] in Christ Jesus our Lord.
